main_body: A flat sand ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a sparse speckle of darker and lighter dots on a single base tone. It is a terrain tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none: the column scan shows only repeating base sand (#dbb26b) with 1-row speckle dots (#c49553, #ebca88, #a5753f). There is no top band or front face, as expected for flat ground.
evidence: This is flat terrain, so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The patch has no standing volume, no receding side face, and no fake front elevation, top-down slab or rim. It is a plain ground texture, which is acceptable for a terrain kind.

style.evidence: The patch has only 5 distinct colours in total, with a median of 5 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile, so the candidate is far below it. Only the paving reference is close, at 7 colours. The sand has a single base tone with sparse 1px dots and a few 3px highlight dashes. The speckle pattern repeats identically every 16px, so the tiling is visible. Shading steps are about 4, against about 6 for Beodeul. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas, and there is no outline. Next to the grass reference it looks thinner and more mechanical, without clumps, grain variation or mid-tone transitions. In doubt, fail.
